title: No test for total_size mismatch after assembly (size= vs actual assembled bytes)
description:
The Assembler accepts a total_size from =ybegin size= and pre-allocates that many bytes. If the parts collectively provide exactly total_size bytes and is_complete() is true, finish() returns the buffer. There is no validation that the decoded data lengths are consistent with each other or with the sum of all part ranges equalling total_size.

More importantly, there is no test that checks what happens when is_complete() returns true but the assembled buffer does not match the declared size= field (e.g., because the caller passed a wrong total_size to Assembler::new). The size= field is caller-supplied and not re-validated inside finish().

This is partially covered by is_complete() checking that all bytes [0, total_size) are covered, but there is no test that supplies a wrong total_size and verifies the assembler rejects or correctly signals the mismatch.
